title: Novel Compound Heterozygous Mutations in the SYNE1 Gene in a Taiwanese Family: A Case Report and Literature Review
case_prompt: A 53-year-old woman from a nonconsanguineous family presented with a 20-year history of progressive unsteady gait, slurred speech, and uncoordinated movements. Neurologic examination revealed pure cerebellar signs, including gaze-evoked nystagmus, saccadic pursuit with hypometric saccades, scanning speech, dysmetria, dysdiadochokinesia, and a wide-based gait. Cranial nerve function was normal, and the Mini-Mental State Examination was within normal limits. Nerve conduction studies, electromyography, and electroencephalography were all normal. Laboratory tests, including renal and liver function, were within normal ranges. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed diffuse cerebellar atrophy.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Secondary causes excluded — “Her medical history eliminated the possibility of trauma, infection, toxicity, primary or metastatic tumor, excess alcohol consumption, vitamin deficiency, and immune-mediated disorders that may cause secondary ataxia.”  
2. Sporadic spinocerebellar ataxia (SCA) considered — “Based on the patient’s clinical features (late onset at nearly 30 years of age with a slowly progressing pattern of nearly 20 years duration), we first considered a diagnosis of sporadic spinocerebellar ataxia (SCA).”  
3. CAG-repeat SCA panel negative — “We used a gene panel to screen for CAG-repeat expansion SCA, but the results were negative.”  
4. Friedreich’s ataxia deprioritized — “We did not test for Friedreich’s ataxia because this disease is extremely rare in the East Asian population.”  
5. Whole exome sequencing diagnostic — “Therefore, we used WES and identified the SYNE1 mutations associated with ARCA. Given the patient’s clinical manifestations, a diagnosis of ARCA1 was finally established.”
